subject: SLA remedy escrow and exception carveout — proposal walkthrough
messages:
From: Megan Li <megan.li@novacloud.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 1 Oct 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SLA remedy escrow and uptime baseline — follow-up

Karthik —

Thanks again for the demo last week. One follow-up item from our infra team: we need clearer language in the SLA around monthly remedy (credits) and an escrow-style reconciliation so we can report to our CFO. High level asks from NovaCloud:

- Baseline uptime target: 99.95% for production API (this is non-negotiable for our customer SLAs).
- Monthly remedy schedule: if availability falls below 99.95, credits should start at 5% of monthly fees for the first band (99.9–99.95), then 15% for 99.5–99.9, max cumulative 50% per month.
- Maintenance carveout: define planned maintenance window and a <<maintenance credit cap>>; we need maintenance to be constrained to 8 hours/month for hosted tiers and advance notice of 72 hours.
- Escrow/reconciliation: we want a simple monthly reconciliation report and an escrow mechanism (credit balance that can be applied to future invoices or refunded).

I attached a short appendix (Proposed_SLA_Appendix_Nova_v2.pdf) with our suggested bands and an example calculation. Can you confirm which items Redwood can accept and where you need exceptions? If helpful let's set a quick 30-minute call.

Thanks —
Megan Li
Head of Infrastructure, NovaCloud
megan.li@novacloud.com

--
Attachment: Proposed_SLA_Appendix_Nova_v2.pdf (pdf, 84KB)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Megan Li <megan.li@novacloud.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 2 Oct 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA remedy escrow and uptime baseline — follow-up

Megan —

Appreciate the clear appendix. Internal summary below and a pragmatic counterproposal. We're generally aligned on transparency — the differences are primarily around baseline and the monthly cap. Short answer: Redwood's hosted default is 99.9% availability; Dedicated customers often get 99.95% SLAs. For the hosted API (the product you plan to use initially) we can propose a committed path to 99.95% within 60 days of go-live (operational validation), but the signed baseline has to reflect the current deployment mode.

Counterproposal (high level):
- Baseline: 99.9% committed at contract signature for hosted, with an operational upgrade path to 99.95% after an initial stabilization window (30–60 days) and validated traffic profile.
- Remedy bands: we can accept the banded approach you proposed but ask that the cumulative monthly cap be 75% for the first 6 months, then reassess. Reason: immediate 50% cap is high for hosted multi-tenant runs.
- Maintenance carveout: Redwood can commit to 8 hours/month for critical scheduled maintenance with 72-hour notice for changes that affect production-level endpoints. For non-critical, we'll notify 48 hours.
- Escrow/reconciliation: we support monthly reconciliation reports and offering credit balances applied to the next invoice. We do not typically do cash refunds for hosted usage unless under special circumstances.

I've attached a draft (Redwood_SLA_Remedy_Draft.docx) with redlineable language. Next steps I propose:
1) Laura (rev ops) to confirm billing mechanics for credit application.
2) Ben (legal) to provide concise language we can send to NovaCloud legal for review.
3) If NovaCloud is comfortable, sign an addendum with a 60-day operational validation clause for the 99.95 upgrade.

Would you be open to the 75% temporary cap as a middle ground? If yes, we can route a redline. Otherwise we can propose a pilot where we guarantee 99.95 for the critical route(s) only.

Thanks,
Karthik
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

--
Attachment: Redwood_SLA_Remedy_Draft.docx (docx, 24KB)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>

Date: Sun, 3 Oct 2027 08:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA remedy escrow and uptime baseline — legal notes (short)

Quick notes from legal:
- Maintenance carveout: prefer 12 hours/month (industry standard) but can accept 8 hours if we tighten the definition of "maintenance" to planned, announced, and limited to non-peak windows.
- Remedy cap: prefer to keep a monthly cap of 100% as a backstop for catastrophic failures; can agree to a commercial cap of 75% for hosted if NovaCloud accepts a quarterly review and an emergency remediation clause (we get to prioritize mitigation actions).
- Escrow: DocuSign amendment for credit-application preferred. If NovaCloud insists on refunds, need explicit refund triggers and CFO approval.

I'll prepare a concise redline and include a DocuSign envelope link when ready.

-Ben
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: SLA remedy escrow and uptime baseline — follow-up

Karthik / Ben / Laura —

Thanks for the thoughtful response and for looping in legal/ops. Quick responses to your points:

- We can consider a 75% commercial cap as a short-term compromise only if the 99.95 baseline is contractually guaranteed from day one for the production API. The operational upgrade path doesn't work for us due to downstream SLOs with our customers.
- We are OK with credit application to the next invoice (no cash refund required) but insist on an escrow-style monthly statement that our finance team can reconcile automatically (CSV or SFTP).
- Maintenance: 8 hours/month is acceptable — but we require blackout windows (US east 08:00–20:00 local) unless explicit prior written consent.

We are trying to avoid a long back-and-forth. If Redwood can sign to 99.95 day-one for the production route and accept a 75% cap with an automated monthly escrow statement, we can move forward this week. Otherwise we will ask our procurement team to underwrite a dedicated pool for higher availability.

Proposed next step: short call tomorrow (Oct 6) 09:00–09:30 PT to finalize language.

Thanks —
Megan

Subject: Re: SLA remedy escrow and uptime baseline — proposal walkthrough (finalizing)

Megan —

Thanks — appreciate the clarity. We're willing to accept the following final commercial terms to close quickly:

- Baseline: Redwood will commit to 99.95% availability for the production API as of contract effective date for the scope of endpoints defined in Appendix A (critical routes). Non-critical endpoints remain at 99.9% until validated.
- Remedy bands and cap: credits applied monthly as follows: 99.95–99.9 = 5% credit; 99.9–99.5 = 15% credit; <99.5 = 40% credit. Cumulative cap for hosted production routes: 75% per month for first 3 months, then move to 50% thereafter (subject to quarterly review).
- Maintenance carveout: 8 hours/month permitted; Redwood will avoid US East peak window 08:00–20:00 local unless agreed in writing.
- Escrow/reconciliation: Redwood will provide an automated monthly CSV statement (SFTP or secure link) with a credit balance that will be applied to the next invoice. No automatic cash refunds; exception workflow documented in the amendment.
- Operational validation: 14-day validation window after contract signature to confirm traffic profile on the production endpoints defined in Appendix A. If validation fails, the 99.95 commitment converts to a documented remediation plan with milestone dates.

Attached: SLA_Final_Proposal_20271005.pdf (editable) with the redlined language. If this matches NovaCloud's legal view, Ben will prepare the DocuSign envelope and Laura will confirm billing instructions for credit application.

If you confirm, we'll schedule the 09:00 PT call tomorrow and have internal pre-call materials ready.

Best,
Karthik
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
